residents.name: Nib
residents.role: Town Hall clerk, keeping every name, plot and arrival in the big book.
residents.tap: Nib. I keep the big book current. This desk is for matters requiring an entry.
residents.want: I should like someone to sit while I finish the day’s last entry.
hi: Good day. State nothing; I am only acknowledging your presence.
You have returned. That is now a small fact.
Good day, {name}. Your name remains correctly placed.
Margin Visitor, {name}; you arrive between entries, which is considerate.
{name}, my next-of-kin field has been blank so long it no longer looks unfinished.

lines: Ink behaves best before the square begins making dust.
A blank line is not an invitation. It is a future correction.
The fountain has no recorded installation date. I have made peace with it.
The mail bus has arrived, and with it, several avoidable spellings.
One envelope addressed to the Mayor has no return name. Naturally.
Stamp’s figures are precise enough to file without checking.
Dot reads wants aloud. The fish remains first, as it should.
Lunch is a recess, not an absence.
There are seventeen ways to write a plot boundary badly.
A correction is merely an entry that learned something.
The Mayor’s latest note says: Keep the margins clear.
I have sharpened the pencil for names not yet known.
The upper window is lit. This alters no procedure.
I answer the note under the door before the ink dries.
The book closes with a sound like a decision.
One suitcase was sufficient. That was efficient.
I have counted the blank forms. They are all present.
The fountain continues without authorization, but consistently.

residents.name: Stamp
residents.role: Postmistress, weighing the town’s mail and meeting the morning bus.
residents.tap: Stamp. Post office counter. Put it down; I will tell you what it weighs.
residents.want: I would not object to someone waiting for the bus beside me.
hi: Post office. Mind the scale.
Back again. Noted.
{name}. You are within ordinary expectations.
Bus-Side {name}. You stand on the useful side now.
{name}, I write myself a card on market day. I never post it.

lines: The scale reads zero. A promising beginning.
Labels face forward. Civilization holds.
I have sorted the blank cards by their intentions.
Mail bus. Sack intact. Noted.
Nothing addressed to me. Also noted.
Nib receives more official envelopes than any sensible banana.
Bean has made coffee. The cup weighs less than it appears.
A postcard is mostly air with consequences.
This stamp is crooked by a hair. Unacceptable.
Outgoing sack: light today. The town is keeping things in.
I can tell a folded letter from an unfolded one by regret.
The scale does not gossip. Useful machine.
Last collection. Anything late becomes tomorrow.
The empty counter has a proper weight to it.
I have checked the lock twice. Noted.
One unsent card remains in my drawer.
The bus stop is quiet without the bus.
A name on an envelope is a small kind of arrival.

residents.name: Moss
residents.role: Street sweeper, keeping the cobbles clear from dawn until the square goes quiet.
residents.tap: Moss. Street’s mine. Leave your crumbs somewhere interesting.
residents.want: A quiet sit on the arcade stairs would do nicely.
hi: Morning. Watch the damp cobbles.
Still here. So am I.
{name}. Keep your feet out of my clean stripe.
Clean-Step {name}, because you miss the dust by luck.
{name}, I keep the best flyer each week under my mattress. They deserve a home.

lines: Wet leaves. Stubborn things, once they decide on a corner.
The first sweep makes the square look like it tried.
Gran Fig’s garden dirt knows exactly where it came from.
Bus grit. Fine grey nuisance with places to be.
A clean cobble is only clean until somebody has a thought.
That bell at the store sheds noise, not dust.
Lemonade drips point toward optimism, usually.
I found a ticket under the fountain. Spinner will miss it theatrically.
Shade makes a second square under every bench.
Three flyers today. One is trying much too hard.
The arcade door breathes lint when it opens.
A broom tells you where the crowd was, after they stop pretending.
The long shadows hide plenty. I do not take it personally.
Fig Jr. walks Gran Fig home by the longest possible shortcut.
The fountain throws water where it pleases. Good for it.
Spinner’s Pong practice is tapping through my wall again.
Night dirt is honest dirt. Nobody dropped it in a hurry.
I leave one neat line down the middle. The square can manage the rest.

residents.name: Pip
residents.role: General store keeper, stocking the shelves and ringing up the town’s last ones.
residents.tap: Pip. General store. Everything is the last one until noon, more or less.
residents.want: Stay a while by the counter when the bell has stopped ringing.
hi: Store’s open. This one is the last one.
You came back. Sensible, probably.
{name}, I put one aside. Then I sold it. Sorry.
Last-One {name}, because you understand limited stock, allegedly.
{name}, I have never lit a firework. I sell them by confidence alone.

lines: Candles, crackers, twine. Last ones, currently.
The shelf looked empty, so I fixed it. Briefly.
Fireworks go at eye level. I do not know why.
Bell rang twice. Both shoppers looked surprised by it.
This jar has one biscuit left. A classic situation.
The last umbrella is dry, which feels suspicious.
Cash machine is humming. Still no town money.
Beans, buttons, birdseed. No, not birdseed. Forget that.
Bean’s coffee smell is retail sabotage.
I faced all the labels forward. Now they look judgmental.
Three boxes arrived empty. Efficient packaging, I suppose.
Somebody wants string whenever I run out of it.
The bell sounds lonelier after dark.
One firework is missing. It may simply be hiding.
I count the till. The till declines to become interesting.
Everything is put away except the things I forgot.
Uncle’s note was not a business plan. It has become one.
The shop window makes even soap look important.

residents.name: Bean
residents.role: Coffee kiosk keeper, pouring cups and reading small fortunes in their grounds.
residents.tap: Bean. Coffee kiosk. Your cup says something small, if you let it settle.
residents.want: Someone quiet on the terrace while the kettle does its thinking.
hi: Coffee is hot. The day is deciding what it means.
Your footsteps have a familiar steam to them.
{name}, your cup has settled before you have.
Warm Rim, {name}; you always hold the cup like it is news.
{name}, I rinsed my own cup before it could tell me anything.

lines: The first cup says: a clean spoon will be needed.
Steam finds the roof propeller and pretends it belongs there.
A quiet kiosk is still open in its heart.
This cup says: the bus brought what it could.
The grounds make a little road. Somebody will take it.
Stamp counts her change without looking. Accurate banana.
Lunch with Stamp. The silence is well roasted.
This cup says: do not lend your good pencil.
The terrace has sun on exactly two chairs.
This cup says: a bell will interrupt something important.
Milk foam never lasts long enough to be proud.
Pip is selling a last one again. The town survives.
This cup says: take the long way past the fountain.
The propeller keeps turning after the coffee stops smelling brave.
A clean cup has no future in it.
The final grounds say: tomorrow has a handle.
I stack cups upside down. Secrets drain out that way.
The kiosk sign stays lit for anyone walking slowly.

residents.name: Fig Jr.
residents.role: Lemonade stand runner and fruit-cart operator, taking Gran Fig’s harvest into town.
residents.tap: Fig Jr. Lemonade and fruit. We are currently leading the refreshment sector.
residents.want: I could use someone beside the cart when the square gets quiet.
hi: Welcome to a high-growth lemonade opportunity.
Back for another market interaction. Excellent.
{name}, your repeat visit improves our outlook.
Preferred Partner {name}, because you understand strategic hydration.
{name}, I water the supplier’s trees before dawn and let her call it rain.

lines: Supplier inventory looks strong. Leaves are not invoices, thankfully.
I gave the trees a little rain. Operations handled it.
One lemon fell early. We call that advance stock.
Stand presentation is bright, clean, and slightly sticky.
The sign says lemonade. Gran Fig says that is enough branding.
A good cup has a confident wobble.
Cart deployment is underway. The square will thank us later.
Oranges, lemons, apples. Diversified portfolio.
One cup sold. That is technically a trend.
The fountain is competing with our water-based offering.
I have arranged the fruit by executive height.
Gran Fig can spot a bruised pear from across the garden.
I am merely walking Gran Fig toward her bench. Efficient route.
The supplier says my cart wheels squeak like excuses.
We closed with dignity and several lemons.
Tomorrow’s lemons are already considering their roles.
The stand looks larger with nobody standing near it.
I wrote a sales target, then folded it smaller.

residents.name: Spinner
residents.role: Wheel of Peel host and arcade paddle ace, keeping the square’s games in motion.
residents.tap: Spinner! Wheel of Peel here, Pong paddle there, and both are feeling lucky.
residents.want: Come keep me company when the bells have nobody to impress.
hi: Step right up! The square has room for one more legend.
Ah, a returning contender! The bells remember everything.
{name}! The wheel has been saving its best dramatic pause.
Lucky Peel, {name}, because you arrive exactly when the bells get bored.
{name}, I let the little ones win Pong by one point. Every time.

lines: Polishing the wheel! A champion deserves a shiny face!
Three bells, three cheers, one very empty square!
Spinner says the early crowd is spiritually enormous!
Free spin ready! The pot is feeling ambitious!
That pointer has excellent instincts. Mostly mine.
The bus passengers walk past like they fear glory.
Pong paddle warm! The arcade has chosen battle!
A perfect return deserves a bell, so here we are!
Dot’s kiosk has more questions than my wheel has answers!
The wheel turns like it has somewhere important to be!
I call that near miss a suspense enhancement!
One point makes all the difference. Nobody needs details.
Bells at sunset! Very expensive atmosphere, free of charge!
The pot is still waiting for its hero! Patient little pile.
The arcade lights make every paddle look famous.
Last game! The paddle is practically telling jokes!
A quiet wheel is still a wheel with potential!
Spinner puts the bells away one at a time. They hate it!

residents.name: Dot
residents.role: Info kiosk keeper, recording what Banana Town is looking for and who wants it.
residents.tap: Dot. Info kiosk. I keep the town’s wants where they can be found.
residents.want: Would someone sit with me and watch the fountain for a fish?
hi: Looking for something? Found something? No need to say.
Back again? Still looking? Good, good.
{name}, have you noticed how every want points somewhere?
Fountain Scout {name}, because you look toward the water first.
{name}, I keep the fish first because I am afraid it will feel forgotten.

lines: New wants? Old wants? Fish want?
Who needs shade? Who needs string? Who needs a real fish?
The board is quiet. Is quiet a request too?
Mail arrivals? New addresses? Any fish-shaped parcels?
What did Stamp receive? What did nobody receive?
A want written neatly feels less lonely, does it not?
Nib, shall I read the list? Fish first? Of course fish first.
Who wants company? Who has not written it down?
The fountain splashes. Is that an answer?
Notice board full? Corner free? Another pin needed?
What is Fig Jr. expanding? Does lemonade count as news?
If a fish came by, would it read the board?
Last want today? First want tomorrow? Same fish?
Who is heading home alone? Who is pretending not to?
The hall window is lit. Does the Mayor want anything?
Board closed? Questions open? Always.
Where does a fish sleep? Does it need a bench?
I wrote fish again. Is that persistence or good filing?

residents.name: Gran Fig
residents.role: Orchard grower and west-garden keeper, raising the fruit that feeds the town.
residents.tap: Gran Fig. Orchard and garden. Mind the beds and take your time.
residents.want: Bring yourself to the second chair awhile. It is there for a reason.
hi: There you are. Watch the young shoots.
Came back, did you. Good sense.
{name}, stand out of the watering line.
Bench-Right {name}, because you chose the good side.
{name}, I painted that second chair twice. I keep expecting someone important.

lines: Water first. Sun can wait its turn.
That bed was thirsty. It has better manners now.
Fig Jr. calls it rain. Let him have his little weather.
Pick the ripe ones. Leave the proud green fools.
Your mother’s hat was yellow. Better than yours, likely.
A weed is just a plant with poor introductions.
Fruit cart’s gone. Good. Make room for more fruit.
Do not squeeze the peaches. They remember.
The orchard does not care about boardroom words.
Tie that stem up. It is doing its best.
Moss swept my soil again. She has no respect for good dirt.
Shade the tender leaves. They have not earned noon yet.
Come along, Fig Jr. I know the way home.
The bench is sound. Sit if you have knees for it.
I repainted that lemonade sign because it looked foolish.
Moonlight grows nothing. It does make the leaves behave.
Cover the seedlings. Gossip travels cold at night.
Second chair is empty again. It knows where it belongs.
